readers.program: libpos, the real FPGA driver (rinzler, runtron, hardware tests)
readers.mechanism: getenv in pos_startup_host. The text goes to tron::hardware::system::system_parse_env (src/system/system.cpp:2112)

readers.mechanism: getenv in pos_startup_host. The text goes to tron::hardware::system::system_parse_env

readers.program: libsystem: early_parse_instance (rinzler at src/rinzler.cpp:4563, runtron at src/runtron.cpp:489) and get_sub_instances (tests)
readers.mechanism: std::getenv in parse_instance_from_system_config. Only the --instance option is taken

readers.program: libsystem: system_parse_args (rinzler at src/rinzler.cpp:4046, runtron at src/runtron.cpp:248)
readers.mechanism: std::getenv. Reached only when DICE_DAEMON_CHILD is 1

setters.value: the submitted SYSTEM_CONFIG merged with --instance for the granted slots
setters.why: the Dice daemon passes the granted instance to the child process

setters.value: --instance <id>,<count>
setters.why: Slice runs each test on its own instance

setters.value: --instance <value of the --instance flag>
setters.why: the reproduction script selects the instance for the child

variables.values: Text in command-line form. It is split at white space. A token in double quotes may hold spaces, and a backslash escapes a quote or a backslash inside the quotes (std::quoted, src/system/system.cpp:2074-2081). Recognised options (src/system/system.cpp:1954-2052): --instance x,y (also --instance=x,y, where x is the instance number from 0, y is the instance count, and x < y), --devices LIST, --app-cores LIST, --dev-cores LIST, --helper-cores LIST, --numa N, --nr_hugepages N, --hugepage_file PATH, --resource-map PATH, --tracer-core N, --kv-cache-gb N, -o or --optimize, --no-opt, --heap-shadow. A token -- ends the parse. Any other token is ignored without a message. Outside a Dice grant the form --option=value is accepted only for --instance. Under a Dice grant (DICE_DAEMON_CHILD=1) the form --option=value is accepted for every option that takes a value (src/system/system.cpp:1877-1880).
variables.default: Unset: the startup code does not parse it. Only the system options from the command line apply. Exception: when DICE_DAEMON_CHILD is 1, an unset or empty value makes startup fail, because --instance is then required. Empty and DICE_DAEMON_CHILD not 1: the text is parsed as an empty option list.
variables.effect: Gives the system placement options to the process through the environment. --instance selects which share (FPGA cards, CPU cores, NUMA node, hugepage files) of the server this process owns. pos_startup_host parses the variable after the command line was parsed, so an option given here replaces the same option from the command line.
variables.notes: 1. Second use: rinzler and runtron call early_parse_instance at program start (src/rinzler.cpp:4563, src/runtron.cpp:489). That call reads --instance from this variable only when the command line has no --instance (src/system/system.cpp:1024-1027). rinzler uses the result for the log line prefix and for the FUSE stats mount directory. runtron uses it for the FUSE stats mount directory. 2. A bad value makes system_parse_env return false. pos_startup_host then logs 'INIT: invalid SYSTEM_CONFIG' and returns -1. With the real driver, get_devices then exits the process with status 1 (src/pos/driver.cpp:887-889). Causes: --instance not in the form x,y, two --instance options, an empty or badly formed device list (each entry has the form e1:00.0: three hexadecimal numbers of 1 or 2 digits, src/system/system.cpp:323-343), an empty CPU list, an option that needs a value at the end of the text. 3. Numbers have no error handling. The values of --numa, --nr_hugepages, --tracer-core and --kv-cache-gb are parsed with std::stoi or std::stoull (src/system/system.cpp:2022-2047). Non-numeric text there throws a C++ exception, and pos_startup_host is noexcept (src/pos/driver.cpp:191), so the process ends. The numbers inside CPU lists are parsed with std::stoi inside parse_cpu_list, which is itself noexcept (src/system/system.cpp:388-405). Non-numeric text in a CPU list therefore ends the process on every path, also when the option comes from the command line. Under a Dice grant a bad CPU list is rejected earlier with a 'Dice grant' error (dice_cpu_list, src/system/system.cpp:1561-1582). 4. Each parse outside a Dice grant reloads the resource map (src/system/system.cpp:1935). The path for that reload comes only from the text being parsed. So when SYSTEM_CONFIG is set and does not repeat --resource-map, a --resource-map from the command line is dropped and the default search order is used. 5. The hugepage count from --nr_hugepages is replaced later by POS_1GB_PER_NUMA or POS_NR_HUGEPAGES, and --hugepage_file by POS_HUGEPAGE_PATH (src/pos/driver.cpp:249-288). 6. Under a Dice grant (DICE_DAEMON_CHILD=1) the command line and this variable are checked together against the granted slots before any option is applied. The --instance here must equal the instance that DICE_SLOTS describes (src/system/system.cpp:2086-2102). 7. Setter sites listed are examples from outside this area. The regular-expression scan of the checkout lists 30 setter sites.

variables.name: POS_1GB_PER_NUMA

readers.program: libpos, the real FPGA driver (rinzler, runtron, hardware tests)
readers.mechanism: getenv, then atoi

setters.why: a Dice test checks that the daemon passes the variable on to the child process

variables.values: Integer parsed with atoi: the number of 1 GiB hugepages for each NUMA node of the server. The code counts one NUMA node per CPU package (socket). Non-numeric text is read as 0. There is no range check.
variables.default: Unset: POS_NR_HUGEPAGES is used when it is set. Otherwise the count is the --nr_hugepages value, or 16 hugepages (default_n_hugepages, h/system/config.hpp:12).
variables.effect: Sets how many 1 GiB hugepages the process maps for its DMA heap (the memory that the FPGA cards read and write). With --instance: pages = value x NUMA node count / 8 x slices owned by this instance, in integer arithmetic (src/pos/driver.cpp:260). Without --instance: pages = value.
variables.notes: Wins over POS_NR_HUGEPAGES and over --nr_hugepages from the command line or SYSTEM_CONFIG. The NUMA node count in the formula is get_num_numa_nodes(), which counts CPU packages (sockets) in the hwloc topology (src/system/system.cpp:300-307). The divisor 8 is the constant n_slices (h/system/system.hpp:212). The result is capped by the locked-memory limit of the process (RLIMIT_MEMLOCK in GiB, src/pos/driver.cpp:277-281). With --instance that limit is first rounded down to a multiple of the slices owned. A negative value becomes a very large unsigned count, which the same cap then lowers to the limit. The comment at src/system/huge.cpp:64-72 names this variable as the one to use in production. When no KV cache size is given, the default KV cache size is half of the hugepage count (src/system/system.cpp:2539-2545). Not read by pos_fake programs (rinzler_proxy). doc/dice.md:859 says the Dice daemon passes this variable on to its child processes.

variables.name: POS_NR_HUGEPAGES

readers.program: libpos, the real FPGA driver (rinzler, runtron, hardware tests)
readers.mechanism: getenv, then atoi

setters.value: the value of the script's hugepage argument
setters.why: the reproduction script sizes the heap of the child

variables.values: Integer parsed with atoi: the total number of 1 GiB hugepages for this process. Non-numeric text is read as 0. There is no range check.
variables.default: Unset: the count is the --nr_hugepages value, or 16 hugepages (default_n_hugepages, h/system/config.hpp:12).
variables.effect: Sets how many 1 GiB hugepages the process maps for its DMA heap (the memory that the FPGA cards read and write).
variables.notes: Ignored when POS_1GB_PER_NUMA is set (else-if at src/pos/driver.cpp:272). Wins over --nr_hugepages from the command line or SYSTEM_CONFIG. The result is capped by the locked-memory limit of the process (RLIMIT_MEMLOCK in GiB, src/pos/driver.cpp:277-281). A negative value becomes a very large unsigned count, which the same cap then lowers to the limit. With --instance the final count must divide evenly by the number of slices owned, or an assertion fails (src/system/huge.cpp:665-666). The comment at src/system/huge.cpp:65 and 71 calls this variable deprecated. That comment spells it POS_NR_HUGEPAGE. The code reads POS_NR_HUGEPAGES. Not read by pos_fake programs (rinzler_proxy).

variables.name: POS_HUGEPAGE_PATH

readers.program: libpos, the real FPGA driver (rinzler, runtron, hardware tests)
readers.mechanism: getenv. The text becomes the global hugepage_file

readers.program: libpos, the real FPGA driver (rinzler, runtron, hardware tests)
readers.mechanism: getenv. The path is checked by dice_validate_hugepage_path (a check that only acts when DICE_DAEMON_CHILD is 1)

readers.program: libsystem: dice_parse_arguments (rinzler, runtron, rinzler_proxy, tests), reached only when DICE_DAEMON_CHILD is 1
readers.mechanism: std::getenv. The path is checked by dice_validate_hugepage_path

setters.value: a path equal to /dev/hugepages/libpos after normalisation
setters.why: the test checks the Dice grant path check

variables.values: Path of a file on a hugetlbfs mount (a file system that hands out hugepages). The text is used as given.
variables.default: Unset: the path from --hugepage_file (command line or SYSTEM_CONFIG), or /dev/hugepages/libpos (default_hugepage_file, h/system/config.hpp:6). An empty value is not treated as unset: the path becomes empty. not determined: the result of an empty path outside a Dice grant (looked at src/pos/driver.cpp:283-288 and src/system/memory.cpp:137-163).
variables.effect: Sets the base path of the hugepage file that backs the DMA heap. Without --instance the process maps this one file. With --instance only the directory of the path is used: the files are <directory>/slice-<k>-of-8, one for each slice that the instance owns (src/system/huge.cpp:639-643).
variables.notes: Wins over --hugepage_file. Startup cleanup removes unused hugepage files that match this path or its directory (src/system/huge.cpp:97-107, 686-718). Under a Dice grant (DICE_DAEMON_CHILD=1) the path must resolve to the same file as /dev/hugepages/libpos. Another path, or an empty value, fails startup with a 'Dice grant ...: POS_HUGEPAGE_PATH requested ...' error (src/system/system.cpp:1649-1661), and the default path is the one used (src/pos/driver.cpp:286-287). The apply step at src/pos/driver.cpp:283 runs only in the real driver. pos_fake programs only reach the Dice check at src/system/system.cpp:2089. t/t_system.cpp sets it at 2 sites (lines 307 and 309) and unsets it at line 315.

variables.name: TRACE_FILE

readers.program: libpos, the real FPGA driver (rinzler, runtron, hardware tests)
readers.mechanism: getenv. The text becomes tron::perfetto_trace_dest

variables.values: Either the exact text traced, or a file path. The text is not checked at startup.
variables.default: Unset: the trace destination stays traced (src/pos/perf.cpp:34). traced is the Perfetto system daemon. An outside client owns the session.
variables.effect: Sets the process-wide Perfetto trace destination. A SIGUSR1 capture (a 10 second trace that the process starts when it receives signal SIGUSR1, src/pos/perf.cpp:248-291) then writes to that file from inside the process, instead of sending events to the traced daemon.
variables.notes: The file is opened with O_TRUNC and mode 0600 at each capture (src/pos/perf.cpp:173-175), so a new capture replaces the old file. If the file cannot be opened, start_tracing throws inside a noexcept thread and the process ends. An empty value fails the same way (comment at perfetto/tools/rinzler-capture.sh:202-205). The failure happens at the SIGUSR1 signal, not at startup. Only programs with the real driver install the SIGUSR1 tracer (src/pos/driver.cpp:447), and only they read this variable. runtron --trace and --trace-gen write the same global earlier, before the model run starts (src/runtron.cpp:263, 295), and the runtron trace takes its destination at that point (src/runtron.cpp:267, 342). pos_startup_host runs later, at the first get_devices call, and then this variable replaces the global. So in runtron the variable changes only the destination of later SIGUSR1 captures. That order was read from src/runtron.cpp, which belongs to another area. README.perfetto.md:206-212 describes the variable. Two tests read the same name with their own getenv (t/t_gof_staging_leaks.cpp:74, t/t_pos_lifecycle_fake.cpp:200). Those files belong to another sweep. No setter was found in the checkout.

variables.name: TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES

readers.program: libpos and pos_fake (rinzler, runtron, rinzler_proxy, rinzler_mock, rinzler_host, tests)
readers.mechanism: std::getenv(trace_categories_variable) in trace_categories_spec. The constant holds the name and is defined at h/common/perfetto.hpp:243

readers.program: libpos and pos_fake (rinzler, runtron, rinzler_proxy, rinzler_mock, rinzler_host, tests)
readers.mechanism: call of trace_categories_spec in local_trace_config. Used when the caller gives no category text

readers.program: libpos and pos_fake (rinzler, runtron, rinzler_proxy, rinzler_mock, rinzler_host, tests)
readers.mechanism: call of trace_categories_spec in require_no_trace_category_override. start_tracing calls it when the destination is traced

setters.value: the category text under test
setters.why: the test sets and restores the variable around each case

variables.values: Comma-separated list of entries. Each entry is +name (record the category) or -name (do not record it). name is a registered category, or the start of one followed by *. The text is not trimmed, so a space before or after an entry makes the entry bad. Registered categories (h/common/perfetto.hpp:103-138): rinzler, sys, scheduler, model, model-moe, matmul, loading, driver, driver-detail, gen, hwattention, hwattention-detail, hw, memory.
variables.default: Unset or empty: no category selection is sent and the Perfetto defaults apply. The comment at h/common/perfetto.hpp:245-249 says a category is then recorded unless it is tagged debug or slow (driver-detail is tagged slow, memory is tagged debug).
variables.effect: Selects which trace categories an in-process trace records. An in-process trace is one that the process writes to a file itself: runtron --trace FILE, a SIGUSR1 capture when TRACE_FILE names a file, or a FUSE capture that gives no category text of its own.
variables.notes: The variable is read at each trace start (start_tracing at src/pos/perf.cpp:165, local_trace_config at src/pos/perf.cpp:144). A bad entry (empty, no + or - sign, * not at the end, no matching category) makes the trace start throw std::invalid_argument (src/pos/perf.cpp:92-124). When the destination is traced (the Perfetto daemon) and the variable is set and not empty, start_tracing throws (src/pos/perf.cpp:126-134), because the daemon takes its categories from its own config file. In the SIGUSR1 capture thread this ends the process (perfetto/tools/rinzler-capture.sh:202-207). A FUSE capture that passes its own category text replaces this variable for that capture (src/pos/trace_capture.cpp:460-461). A plain search for getenv with a quoted name does not find this variable, because the name is held in a constant.

variables.name: TRON_HW_SAMPLER

readers.program: libpos and pos_fake (rinzler, runtron, rinzler_proxy, rinzler_mock, rinzler_host, tests)
readers.mechanism: std::getenv in sampler_opted_in

setters.why: the test turns the sampler on for the case
the lifecycle test needs a sampler thread

variables.values: Exactly the text 1 or the text true enables it. Any other value is off.
variables.default: Unset: the sampler thread is never created and a trace holds no hw counters.
variables.effect: Turns on the hardware telemetry sampler. When a trace session starts, the process creates one background thread. While the trace records the hw category, the thread reads CPU temperature (hwmon), CPU frequency (cpufreq) and package power (RAPL) from sysfs and writes them to the trace as counters.
variables.notes: The read happens at a call of enable_hw_sampling only while no sampler thread exists (spawn_hw_sampler_locked, src/pos/hwperf.cpp:151-152). After the thread exists the variable is not read again. enable_hw_sampling is called from start_tracing (src/pos/perf.cpp:197) and from the FUSE capture path (src/pos/trace_capture.cpp:612). The code comment at src/pos/hwperf.cpp:122-125 gives the reason for off by default: a thread, sysfs reads on every sample, and package power needs wider read access to the RAPL energy files. perfetto/grant-rapl-read tests the same variable before it widens that access (perfetto/grant-rapl-read:24). The sample period is TRON_HW_SAMPLER_INTERVAL_MS.

variables.notes: Has an effect only when TRON_HW_SAMPLER enables the sampler. Read once when the sampler thread starts (src/pos/hwperf.cpp:645). A change after that is not seen by the running thread.

variables.name: TRON_HW_SAMPLER_ALL_SENSORS

readers.program: libpos and pos_fake (rinzler, runtron, rinzler_proxy, rinzler_mock, rinzler_host, tests)
readers.mechanism: std::getenv in sampler_all_sensors

variables.values: Exactly the text 1 or the text true enables it. Any other value is off.
variables.default: Unset: for each CPU socket the trace gets the package temperature and the minimum, average and maximum over the other temperature sensors.
variables.effect: Adds one temperature counter for every single hwmon sensor to the trace, next to the per-socket summary counters.

variables.name: TRON_FIRST_RESULT_WARMUP

readers.program: libpos, the real FPGA driver (rinzler, runtron, hardware tests)
readers.mechanism: std::getenv in warm_up_first_result_fault

setters.value: 0 (only when the variable is not already set)
setters.why: the fault detector test must see the fault that the warm-up would clear
the register test expects reset values that the warm-up would change

variables.values: Exactly the text 0 skips the warm-up. Any other value, also an empty one, leaves it on.
variables.default: Unset: the warm-up runs.
variables.effect: Controls the first-result warm-up. At the first call of get_devices the driver runs one throwaway int4 matrix multiply on each FPGA card and discards the result. Value 0 skips this step and logs 'INIT: first-result warm-up skipped'.
variables.notes: Reason for the warm-up (Note at src/pos/driver.cpp:799-816): on some Archer bitfiles the first int4 weight fetch after an FPGA configuration stores corrupted weights, so the first result is wrong. warm_up_first_result_fault is called once per process, from get_devices (src/pos/driver.cpp:906). The warm-up skips cards whose PCI device id is below 0x0011 (src/pos/driver.cpp:838). Not read by pos_fake programs (rinzler_proxy).

variables.name: HWATTN_MAX_B

readers.program: libpos, the real FPGA driver (rinzler, runtron, hardware tests)
readers.mechanism: std::getenv, then atoi, inside a function-local static in maximum_hwattn_batch_size

variables.values: Integer parsed with atoi. Only a value above 0 is used.
variables.default: Unset, 0, negative or non-numeric: the limit is the value computed from the device (the smaller of the metadata limit and maximum_batch_size, src/pos/driver.cpp:1611-1618).
variables.effect: Lowers the largest batch (number of queries in one pass) that hardware attention accepts on a card. The result is min(value, computed limit), so the variable cannot raise the limit.
variables.notes: The model code uses the result as the number of queries per hardware attention pass (h/tron/models/model.hpp:3046-3050), and the worker asserts against it (src/pos/worker.cpp:822-827). The computed limit is at most MAX_B = 32 (h/libpos.hpp:33). The pos_fake version of the function does not read the variable (src/pos/fake.cpp:415-418). No setter and no document were found for it in the checkout. The audience value is a judgement.

variables.name: HWATTN_WLR

readers.program: libpos, the real FPGA driver (rinzler, runtron, hardware tests)
readers.mechanism: hwattn_env_override("HWATTN_WLR"). The helper calls std::getenv(env_name) at src/pos/device.cpp:103 and then atoi

variables.values: Integer parsed with atoi. A value above 0 forces the feature on. Any other set value (0, negative, non-numeric, empty) forces it off.
variables.default: Unset: each card decides from its bitfile version (hwattn_wlr_bitfile_ok, h/pos/device.hpp:780-795): project 01 needs version 05.08 or later. Project 03 needs version 05.08 or later with a release date of 2026-05-18 or later.
variables.effect: Forces hardware attention weight-load reuse (WLR) on or off for every card, without the bitfile check. With WLR on, when an attention command repeats the weight commands of the previous attention command, the worker sends one K and V pair that tells the FPGA to reuse the weights it already loaded (src/pos/worker.cpp:1380-1398).
variables.notes: When set, the driver logs once: 'HW attention: HWATTN_WLR=<value> forces the feature ON|OFF by env flag; the bitfile capability check is bypassed' (src/pos/device.cpp:106-108). The value is read at the first PosDevice::init and kept for the life of the process. Forcing it on for a bitfile that does not support WLR is not guarded by the code. A plain search for getenv with a quoted name does not find this variable, because the name is passed to a helper. No setter was found in the checkout. Not read by pos_fake programs. The audience value is a judgement: the variable is a feature switch, but it bypasses a capability check.

variables.name: TRON_HWATTN_HEAD_TILING

readers.program: libpos, the real FPGA driver (rinzler, runtron, hardware tests)
readers.mechanism: hwattn_env_override("TRON_HWATTN_HEAD_TILING"). The helper calls std::getenv(env_name) at src/pos/device.cpp:103 and then atoi

variables.values: Integer parsed with atoi. A value above 0 forces the feature on. Any other set value (0, negative, non-numeric, empty) forces it off.
variables.default: Unset: each card decides from its bitfile version (hwattn_tiling_bitfile_ok, h/pos/device.hpp:802-808): project 01 or 03 with version 05.09 or later.
variables.effect: Forces hardware attention head tiling on or off for every card, without the bitfile check. With head tiling on, an attention pass that covers more KV shards than fit in EMEM in one pass is sent as one hardware command that handles fewer heads per pass (hwattn_plan_cmd_shape, h/libpos.hpp:205-219). EMEM is the FPGA memory that holds the intermediate Q.K dot products of hardware attention (h/libpos.hpp:128-130). With it off, such a pass is split into several commands.
variables.notes: When set, the driver logs once: 'HW attention: TRON_HWATTN_HEAD_TILING=<value> forces the feature ON|OFF by env flag; the bitfile capability check is bypassed' (src/pos/device.cpp:106-108). The value is read at the first PosDevice::init and kept for the life of the process. The flag is used by the worker (src/pos/worker.cpp:872-874) and by the model planner (h/tron/models/model.hpp:2990-2992, 3057-3061). A plain search for getenv with a quoted name does not find this variable, because the name is passed to a helper. No setter was found in the checkout. Not read by pos_fake programs. The audience value is a judgement, as for HWATTN_WLR.

variables.name: TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR

readers.program: libsystem, reached only through libpos startup (rinzler, runtron, hardware tests)
readers.mechanism: std::getenv, then strcmp with 1, in read_arena_allocator_env. Called from pos_heap_setup (src/system/memory.cpp:174)

readers.program: libsystem: pos_heap_register_fuse_stats (rinzler and its pos_fake builds rinzler_proxy, rinzler_mock and rinzler_host at src/rinzler.cpp:4957, and runtron at src/runtron.cpp:501)
readers.mechanism: call of read_arena_allocator_env, which reads the variable again at src/system/memory.cpp:94

setters.why: CTest runs this test with the arena allocator
CTest runs this test with the arena allocator

setters.value: the allocator value under test
setters.why: the test starts a child process with each allocator

variables.values: Exactly the text 1 selects the arena allocator. Any other set value, also an empty one, selects the legacy allocator.
variables.default: Unset: the build decides. The CMake option TRON_ARENA_ALLOCATOR_DEFAULT_ON is ON by default (src/system/CMakeLists.txt:86), so a default build uses the arena allocator.
variables.effect: Selects the allocator for the DMA heap (the hugepage memory that the FPGA cards read and write): pos_heap_v2, called the arena allocator, or the legacy pos_heap. It also decides whether the FUSE stats files under /rinzler/stats/dma_heap/ are registered: they exist only when the arena allocator is selected.
variables.notes: Two reads. 1. pos_heap_setup runs once in pos_startup_host (src/pos/driver.cpp:290), so the allocator choice is fixed for the process. Four helpers in an unnamed namespace (lines 126, 170, 179, 184). Each reads one fixed name: TRON_HW_SAMPLER, TRON_HW_SAMPLER_INTERVAL_MS, TRON_HW_SAMPLER_SYSFS_ROOT, TRON_HW_SAMPLER_ALL_SENSORS. Callers: lines 152, 645, 644 and 522 of the same file.

Static helper. Returns true when TRON_NO_RTM is exactly 1. Caller: the initialiser of the global is_rtm_supported (src/system/mwaitx.cpp:57-59). The type tron::lazy runs its initialiser in its constructor (h/common/util.hpp:199-205), so the read happens at static initialization.

Reads TRON_LOG_DIR (line 76), then calls init_logging(path) (line 35), which reads TRON_LOG_LEVEL (line 39) and calls spdlog::cfg::load_env_levels (line 60, reads SPDLOG_LEVEL inside spdlog). Callers: src/pos/driver.cpp:198, src/rinzler.cpp:4547, src/runtron.cpp:439, t/t_chat_template.cpp:420, t/t_rinzler.cpp:193.

dynamic_sites.description: std::getenv(env_name): the name is a parameter of hwattn_env_override. It is not built from pieces. The only names passed are HWATTN_WLR (line 215) and TRON_HWATTN_HEAD_TILING (line 217).
std::getenv(trace_categories_variable): the name comes from a constant, not a literal at the call. The constant is TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES (h/common/perfetto.hpp:243). It is not built from pieces.

notes: Verification of the sweep of area cpp-pos-system. All 121 files of the list were searched again for getenv, secure_getenv, environ, envp, setenv, putenv, unsetenv, clearenv, load_env, exec, spawn, popen and system calls, for every quoted all-capital text, for NAME=value text in comments and help text, and for C library calls that read the environment on their own (temp_directory_path, getpwuid, setlocale, dlopen and similar). Result: 30 names, the same set as the first sweep. No name was added and no name was removed. The helper baseline_only.py printed 0 names that the scan found and the sweep missed. Every getenv call in the area has a literal name, except two: src/pos/device.cpp:103 (two names, both listed) and src/pos/perf.cpp:50 (one constant, listed). A search of src/ and h/ for getenv with a non-literal argument found no other such call. All 30 entries were checked against the code: every reader site, every setter site, and the values, default, effect and when fields. 23 entries were changed. The 'changes' array says for each one whether a fact was wrong or was only made more exact. The two entries with a wrong fact that matters most are TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR (a second reader, reached by the pos_fake programs) and SYSTEM_CONFIG (process end on a bad CPU list, the --option=value form, the lost --resource-map). No file in this area sets, exports or unsets an environment variable, so there is no set_only name. Setter sites come from outside this area and are examples only. Each one listed was opened. Comments that name a variable that nothing reads: src/system/huge.cpp:65-71 spells POS_NR_HUGEPAGE. The code reads POS_NR_HUGEPAGES. Not examined: environment variables that third-party libraries read on their own with no trace in the checkout (hwloc at hwloc_topology_load, src/system/system.cpp:160, libfuse, TBB, libpci, and Perfetto apart from the producer socket name). The library sources are not in the snapshot. Two entries rest on a library read that could not be opened: SPDLOG_LEVEL (spdlog v1.17.0) and PERFETTO_PRODUCER_SOCK_NAME (Perfetto SDK v57.2). Which programs reach each reader: the real driver library pos is linked into rinzler and runtron (through full_scheduler_static, src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:402-408) and into hardware tests. pos_fake is linked into rinzler_proxy, rinzler_mock and rinzler_host (src/CMakeLists.txt:115-194). Readers in src/pos/driver.cpp and src/pos/device.cpp, and pos_heap_setup in src/system/memory.cpp, are therefore not reached by rinzler_proxy. Findings worth a line in the final document: (1) the POS_NR_HUGEPAGE spelling in the huge.cpp comment. (2) HWATTN_WLR and HWATTN_MAX_B have no TRON_ prefix, unlike TRON_HWATTN_HEAD_TILING beside them. (3) SYSTEM_CONFIG numeric options have no error handling for non-numeric text. (4) setting SYSTEM_CONFIG drops a --resource-map given on the command line. (5) TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR is read at two places, and the second one does not use the fixed choice.

changes.name: TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR
changes.detail: Wrong: the entry said pos_heap_setup is the only reader and that pos_fake programs do not read the variable. The code has a second caller of read_arena_allocator_env: pos_heap_register_fuse_stats (src/system/memory.cpp:535). rinzler.cpp calls it at src/rinzler.cpp:4957 with no build guard, so rinzler_proxy, rinzler_mock and rinzler_host read the variable too. runtron calls it at src/runtron.cpp:501, before pos_heap_setup. Added the second reader, the effect on the dma_heap FUSE stats files, a third setter (t/t_pos_lifecycle.cpp:192) and the setter count (10 sites).

changes.name: SYSTEM_CONFIG
changes.detail: Three points. 1. Imprecise: the entry said a bad number in a CPU list ends the process because pos_startup_host is noexcept. parse_cpu_list is itself noexcept (src/system/system.cpp:388-405), so the process ends on every path, also for command-line options. Under a Dice grant dice_cpu_list rejects the list first (src/system/system.cpp:1561-1582). 2. Missing: the form --option=value is accepted only for --instance outside a Dice grant, and for every value option under a Dice grant (src/system/system.cpp:1877-1880). 3. Vague: note 4 now states the result of the resource map reload: a --resource-map from the command line is dropped unless SYSTEM_CONFIG repeats it (src/system/system.cpp:1914-1936). Also replaced 'the other sweeps hold the full list' with the setter count from the scan (30 sites).

changes.name: POS_1GB_PER_NUMA
changes.detail: Imprecise: the entry called the multiplier the NUMA node count. The code uses get_num_numa_nodes(), which counts CPU packages (sockets) in the hwloc topology (src/system/system.cpp:300-307). Wrong: 'no setter was found'. A Dice test passes the variable to a child (bin/dice-tests/test_hardening.py:1061). Added the behaviour of a negative value (n_hugepages is size_t, src/system/system.cpp:44) and the doc/dice.md:859 statement.

changes.name: POS_NR_HUGEPAGES
changes.detail: Added the behaviour of a negative value: it becomes a very large unsigned count and the RLIMIT_MEMLOCK cap lowers it (src/pos/driver.cpp:273-281, src/system/system.cpp:44). No other fact changed.

changes.name: POS_HUGEPAGE_PATH
changes.detail: Added: under a Dice grant an empty value is rejected too (!path.empty() test at src/system/system.cpp:1655). Marked the empty-path result outside a Dice grant as 'not determined' in the required form. Added the count of test sites in t/t_system.cpp.

changes.name: TRACE_FILE
changes.detail: The entry said the order between runtron --trace and this read was not traced. Traced now: runtron writes the global in gen_eval before the model run (src/runtron.cpp:263, 295) and its trace takes the destination at that point (src/runtron.cpp:267, 342, and h/runtron/trace_lifecycle.hpp:14-20). pos_startup_host runs later and then TRACE_FILE replaces the global. Added: only real-driver programs install the SIGUSR1 tracer (src/pos/driver.cpp:447). The failure for a bad path happens at the signal, not at startup.

changes.name: TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES
changes.detail: Made exact: the text is not trimmed. An entry is the text between two commas and must start with + or - (src/pos/perf.cpp:96-102), so a space around an entry makes it bad. No other fact changed.

changes.name: TRON_HW_SAMPLER
changes.detail: Made exact: the variable is read at a call of enable_hw_sampling only while no sampler thread exists (src/pos/hwperf.cpp:152). No other fact changed.

changes.name: TRON_FIRST_RESULT_WARMUP
changes.detail: Added: the warm-up skips cards whose PCI device id is below 0x0011 (src/pos/driver.cpp:838). No other fact changed.

changes.name: SUDO_USER
changes.detail: Made exact: the variable is read only when the effective user id is 0 (short-circuit at src/system/memory.cpp:128). No other fact changed.

changes.name: TRON_NO_RTM
changes.detail: Made exact: the reader is every program that links the system library, also list_devices, because the mwaitx object file is added at the final link (src/system/CMakeLists.txt:36-55). Added: the read is before main, so the variable must be set at launch (tron::lazy runs its initialiser in the constructor, h/common/util.hpp:199-205). 'at static initialization' was confirmed.

changes.name: TRON_LOG_LEVEL
changes.detail: Added the spdlog version that the build downloads (v1.17.0, cmake/versions.cmake:5), so a reader can look up the level names. Changed 'several tests' to the count from the scan (5 test readers). Added that the pos_fake startup does not call init_logging.

changes.name: SPDLOG_LEVEL
changes.detail: Added the spdlog version (v1.17.0, cmake/versions.cmake:5), the README.tokenizers.md:242 mention, and that the read happens only at the first call of init_logging (src/system/spdlog.cpp:36-37).

changes.name: RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH
changes.detail: Added a reader path: rinzler --help calls default_mountpoint to print the default of --fuse-mount (src/rinzler.cpp:4063-4066). Added ExecStopPost to the unit lines that expand the variable (packaging/systemd/rinzler@.service:55).

changes.name: RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PRESCOPED
changes.detail: Added: the variable also applies to the built-in default paths, not only to a path from RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH (src/system/fuse_helpers.cpp:84-87). No other fact changed.

changes.name: REPO_ROOT_OVERRIDE
changes.detail: Wrong wording: the fourth resource map candidate is <directory of the program>/../config/resource-map.yaml, not 'the entry next to the program' (src/system/resource_map.cpp:102-107). Added: under a Dice grant the search is not run (src/system/system.cpp:1930-1936).

changes.name: TRON_HEAP_SHADOW
changes.detail: Replaced 'more tests than the one listed' with the setter count from the scan (7 sites in t/CMakeLists.txt). Added the help text site (h/system/system.hpp:433-434) and the test reader (t/t_kv_accounting_stress.cpp:123).

changes.name: TRON_HEAP_PROFILE_PATH
changes.detail: Made exact: the shadow-map check at src/system/heap_v2.cpp:914 comes before the read, so the variable is not read when the shadow map is off. Added the second test setter site (t/t_heap_v2.cpp:1463).

changes.name: TRON_HW_SAMPLER_ALL_SENSORS
changes.detail: Added the document that describes the variable (README.perfetto.md:482-513). No other fact changed.

changes.name: HWATTN_WLR
changes.detail: Added a note that the audience value is a judgement. No fact changed.

changes.name: TRON_HWATTN_HEAD_TILING
changes.detail: Added a note that the audience value is a judgement. No fact changed.

changes.name: DICE_SLOTS
changes.detail: Made exact: a plus sign is not accepted, because std::from_chars must consume the whole item (src/system/system.cpp:1482-1485). Added: the NUMA node count behind '4 slots per NUMA node' is get_num_numa_nodes(), which counts CPU packages (src/system/system.cpp:300-307, 1181-1182).

changes.name: PERFETTO_PRODUCER_SOCK_NAME
changes.detail: Narrowed the reader: only start_tracing with the destination traced reaches the call at src/pos/perf.cpp:169. Added the Perfetto SDK version (v57.2, cmake/versions.cmake:20). Confidence stays low.

rejected.name: PATH
rejected.reason: bin/iotools-1.5/misc.c:253 calls execvp in the runon command of the vendored iotools program. The C library searches PATH for the command. TRON code does not read the value, and the child gets the environment unchanged. Not listed.

rejected.name: POS_NR_HUGEPAGE
rejected.reason: Named in the comment at src/system/huge.cpp:65-71. No code reads this name. It is a misspelling of POS_NR_HUGEPAGES, which src/pos/driver.cpp:272 reads.

rejected.name: RZ_KV_CACHE_GB
rejected.reason: Named in comments of this area (src/system/system.cpp:85, h/system/system.hpp:353, 361). The read is at src/rinzler.cpp:4575, which belongs to another area. No file of this area reads it.

rejected.name: TMPDIR
rejected.reason: src/pos/trace_capture.cpp:481 states that FUSE capture files always go to /tmp and that TMPDIR is not used. No file of this area reads it.

rejected.name: PERFETTO_CONSUMER_SOCK_NAME
rejected.reason: Used by the Perfetto client scripts under perfetto/ and bin/ci. It names the consumer socket, which the TRON process does not open. No file of this area reads it.

rejected.name: TRON_MWAIT_STATS, TRON_ARENA_ALLOCATOR_DEFAULT_ON, TRON_FUSE_STATS_ENABLED, TRON_SANITIZER, TRON_VERBOSE, TRON_IGNORE_NAN, TRON_IGNORE_FTZ, HEAP_SHADOW, HBM_ALLOC_SHADOW, POS_METRICS_LOG_ENABLED, HW_ALLOCATOR_VERIFY, FAKE_DEVICE, DEBUG_*
rejected.reason: C preprocessor macros or CMake options tested with #ifdef or #if in the files of this area. They are fixed at build time and are not read from the environment.
